description: Specification for the deterministic Eliware validation harness.

authoritativeFor: Harness configuration, bundled-check discovery, check execution, result reporting, and validation safety.
notAuthoritativeFor: Repository requirements, convention wording, profile applicability, exemptions, publication policy, deployment, or operations.

crosslinks.authoritativeFor: Universal repository conventions and profile authority.
Application repository requirements enforced by this package.
CLI repository requirements, public help/version behavior, and exit-code documentation.
npm-published package requirements and the aggregate pack-stage boundary.
Cross-cutting operational procedures and publication/deployment boundaries.

dos: Provide a deterministic Eliware validation harness.
donts: Do not define, reinterpret, duplicate, or extend repository conventions in the harness specification.
Do not perform publication, deployment, synchronization, tagging, pushing, or other external state changes during validation.

dos: Fail fast when required repository configuration is missing or malformed.
donts: Do not begin partial validation with invalid repository configuration.

dos: Read the repository's declared harness configuration before validation begins.
donts: Do not begin check execution before configuration parsing has completed.

dos: Require explicit configuration wherever the harness contract requires it.
donts: Do not infer applicability from repository shape, dependencies, files, scripts, entrypoints, or runtime behavior.
Do not apply an implicit default profile when explicit selection is required.

dos: Keep bundled checks self-contained and organized in profile directories.
donts: Do not require a private external authority repository at runtime.

dos: Discover checks deterministically from the published harness package.
Treat packaged check modules as the runtime authority snapshot.
donts: Do not use a separate runtime registry that can diverge from bundled check modules.

dos: Give every requirement an individually identifiable check module.
donts: Do not combine unrelated requirements into an unidentifiable check.

dos: Make each check's module identity, bundled location, and reported identity agree.
Reject duplicate, malformed, missing, or invalid check identities.
donts: Do not silently overwrite or merge duplicate check identities.

dos: Map each convention check to an existing directive identity in the bundled authority snapshot.
donts: Do not invent a convention requirement from an implementation detail.

dos: Execute applicable bundled architecture checks.
donts: Do not silently skip an applicable bundled architecture check.

dos: The harness must execute every selected deterministic bundled check as part of harness validation.
Preserve each bundled check's pass/fail result and diagnostics.
donts: Do not silently omit a selected deterministic check, or replace a check failure with a warning or successful output.

dos: Keep the harness implementation native ESM, modular, injectable, and covered by its native test suite.
donts: Do not require consumers to import internal harness modules.

dos: Make checks return only pass or fail with stable identities and actionable diagnostics.
donts: Do not expose an undocumented warning, skipped, unknown, or partial state as a passing result.

dos: Report each check independently and aggregate results deterministically.
Preserve failed-check diagnostics without allowing another result to erase them.
donts: Do not silently skip a selected check or convert uncertainty into success.

dos: Keep filesystem traversal, path handling, subprocess execution, and captured diagnostics bounded and platform-neutral.
Invoke child processes with argument arrays and preserve useful failure context.
donts: Do not depend on shell pipelines, shell quoting, platform-specific executable assumptions, or unbounded output capture.
Do not expose sensitive values in harness-owned diagnostics.

dos: Use stable failure categories and deterministic precedence for process results.
donts: Do not change public result semantics as an incidental implementation detail.

dos: Keep validation read-only with respect to external systems and publication state.
donts: Do not publish, release, deploy, synchronize, tag, push, or mutate external state during validation.

dos: Preserve the complete bounded test-process output needed to diagnose failed tests, including both standard output and standard error.
When coverage evidence identifies gaps, report them at file level with each available metric, uncovered lines, and uncovered statement, branch, or function details.
Include concise remediation guidance for every reported coverage gap, including adding or extending tests and refactoring only when needed for testability.
Report missing, malformed, stale, changing, or unusable coverage evidence as a distinct actionable validation failure.
donts: Do not reduce a failed test run to only its exit code or reduce coverage failures to an undifferentiated percentage.
Do not claim complete coverage when detailed evidence is unavailable or unusable.

dos: Support focused testing without silently broadening the requested scope.
donts: Do not replace a focused request with an unrelated broad run.

dos: Expose focused execution through the public eliware-test command.
Validate focused paths and report failures within the requested scope.
donts: Do not require consumers to import internal harness modules to focus a run.

dos: Keep unrelated sources and checks out of focused failure reporting unless explicitly requested.
donts: Do not silently broaden focused validation because a path is difficult to resolve.

dos: Expose only the current public harness commands and diagnostic options: --help, --version, --debug-timing, --ignore-100x4, and --ignore-monolith-limits.
Run the bundled convention-check execution path for a normal invocation and return its stable result and diagnostics through the public CLI contract.
donts: Do not expose direct Jest, Oxlint, npm audit, npm pack, formatter, or other implementation commands as the consumer interface.

dos: Treat --help and --version as informational commands that perform no validation and return exit code 0.
Require explicit convention profile selection in package.json.eliware.apply for normal validation.
Allow diagnostic options to affect only their documented diagnostic or enforcement behavior; they must not select a different profile or invoke an unrelated command.
donts: Do not infer profile applicability from repository shape, files, scripts, dependencies, or runtime behavior.

dos: Keep normal validation limited to bundled convention checks and their orchestration.
Keep publication, deployment, release, synchronization, and external package commands outside the harness runtime.
donts: Do not run unrelated lifecycle stages or invoke the consumer test script recursively.

dos: Allow a recognized focused path with the selected test-related stage and keep discovery, diagnostics, and failures within that requested scope.
Keep stage selection and path focus orthogonal: a focused path does not add stages, and a stage flag does not broaden the path.
Reject unsupported, missing, or ambiguous focused paths with the stable convention failure result before executing unrelated validation.
donts: Do not apply focused-path narrowing to an aggregate package operation or silently reinterpret a package path as a test focus.
Do not fall back to aggregate validation when a focused path cannot be resolved.

dos: Use these stable result categories and exit codes: 0 success, 8 Jest/test failure, 10 coverage failure, 12 lint failure, 14 internal tool/process failure, 17 package-check failure, and 18 convention, configuration, applicability, argument, format, or format-check failure.
Stop before test execution for invalid configuration, unsupported arguments, or inapplicable selected stages; preserve the stable failure result and diagnostics.

After test execution, preserve every failed-stage diagnostic and use the highest applicable post-test exit code as the aggregate result; numeric precedence is an output rule, not a ranking of root-cause severity.
donts: Do not convert an unknown, skipped, partial, or inapplicable selected stage into success.
Do not allow a later result to erase an earlier failure diagnostic or change public exit semantics as an incidental implementation detail.

dos: Make --debug-timing useful for diagnosing slow or hanging tests by streaming timing diagnostics while validation is still running.
Report when each test suite starts so the last reported Running line identifies the suite that may be hanging.
Report each suite's completion and elapsed time as soon as that suite finishes.
Report completed individual test-case durations when the test runner provides them.
Keep live timing output separate from buffered machine-readable results used for coverage and final failure diagnostics.
Run the requested Jest validation as one normal execution with its established ordering, setup, lifecycle, and coverage semantics.
donts: Do not buffer all timing output until the complete validation run exits.
Do not execute every test in a separate process merely to collect timing data.
Do not change test ordering, isolation, setup, coverage enforcement, or exit-code behavior solely because timing diagnostics are enabled.
Do not expose raw machine-readable timing payloads as the normal human-facing timing output.

dos: Monitor test execution progress during every Jest run, whether or not --debug-timing is enabled.
Terminate Jest early when no observable test progress has occurred for 15 seconds.
Report the currently running suite or test when the no-progress watchdog terminates execution, including that it timed out after 15 seconds.
Flag every individual test case that takes longer than 5 seconds, including its suite, test name, and measured duration.
Treat watchdog termination as a test failure with actionable diagnostics while preserving the existing failure result and exit-code contract.
donts: Do not impose a global maximum duration on the complete Jest run.
Do not require --debug-timing for progress monitoring, watchdog termination, or slow-test diagnostics.
Do not terminate an active test merely because it exceeds 5 seconds when progress is still being observed; the 5-second threshold is a diagnostic flag, not the watchdog timeout.
Do not report a watchdog timeout without identifying the last known running suite or test when Jest provides that information.

dos: When validation succeeds without diagnostics, emit exactly one concise human-readable line: All tests passed | 100x4 coverage | 0 lint warnings.
Keep the clean-run line unchanged across normal successful invocations.
donts: Do not emit stage summaries, Jest banners, timing output, subprocess noise, or incidental logs during a normal clean run.
Do not emit the clean-run line when any validation failure or diagnostic is present.

dos: Implement the harness as a self-contained filesystem-discovered convention-check system.
Treat the published bundled checks as the complete runtime authority snapshot.
donts: Do not require the private eliware/conventions repository or any other external authority repository at runtime.
Do not retain a legacy compatibility layer or a second legacy check registry.

dos: Store checks under src/checks/<profile>/ using filenames that are the exact published directive IDs.
Use subdirectories to represent the directive parent/child hierarchy, with the same hierarchy available to exemption traversal.
donts: Do not use a separate mapping.json as the authoritative check registry when profile directories and directive-named modules provide that mapping.

dos: Give each bundled directive module a stable ruleId and a single check entry point that returns a pass or fail result for that exact rule.
Require the module filename, exported identity, and reported result identity to agree.
donts: Do not combine unrelated directive identities into one unidentifiable module or silently treat a malformed module as a passing check.

dos: Provision the bundled check tree from the published convention directive set so that each known directive has a discoverable implementation location.

Keep directives that are not deterministically enforceable from being represented as successful enforcement merely because a scaffold exists; their implementation status must remain distinct from the harness result contract.
donts: Do not claim that a placeholder module enforces a convention before its deterministic check logic exists.

dos: Skip an exempted rule and every discovered child rule beneath that rule before executing check logic.
Validate exemption IDs against the complete bundled check tree, not only the currently selected profiles.
donts: Do not execute a check that is excluded by its applicable exemption or a parent exemption.

dos: Keep applicability selection and exemption evaluation separate from check implementation.
donts: Do not make individual check modules infer their own profile applicability or exemption state.

dos: Treat missing or malformed harness configuration as a fast configuration failure for an in-scope validation target.
donts: Do not begin partial validation with missing or invalid configuration.

dos: Keep focused test execution available through the public harness boundary without reporting unrelated-module coverage failures.
donts: Do not broaden a focused run into unrelated validation.
